name: Question 9
problem: If $\,u(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,v(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]\,$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$, find $Aw(t)$ where $w(t)=[\begin{aligned}-2{e}^{-t} \\ -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
Since $u(t)$ and $v(t)$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
cu(t)+dv(t)
$$

 is also a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for all $c,d\in R.$

Notice that 

$$
w(t)=-2u(t)-v(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $w$ is a solution to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t).$ So, in order to find $Aw(t)$ we just need to find ${w}^{′}(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Aw & ={w}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(-2{e}^{-t})^{′} \\ (-{e}^{t})^{′}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-t} \\ -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

If u(t)=[e−t0] and v(t)=[0et] are solutions to x′(t)=Ax(t), find Aw(t) where w(t)=[−2e−t−et].

a
Aw=[−2e−t−et]
b
Aw=[−e−t−2et]
c
Aw=[et−2e−t]
d
Aw=[2e−tet]
e
Aw=[2e−t−et]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since u(t) and v(t) are solutions to x′(t)=Ax(t), the superposition principle guarantees that cu(t)+dv(t) is also a solution to x′(t)=Ax(t) for all c,d∈R.

Notice that w(t)=−2u(t)−v(t).

Therefore, w is a solution to x′(t)=Ax(t). So, in order to find Aw(t) we just need to find w′(t) as follows:

Aw=w′(t)=[(−2e−t)′(−et)′]=[2e−t−et].
